title: The Hom complex into K-injective complexes respects quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $s:(\mathcal I')^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] between K-injective complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $t:(\mathcal L')^\bullet\to\mathcal L^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Then the morphism of Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex]

$$
 \mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,(\mathcal I')^\bullet)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom^\bullet((\mathcal L')^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet),\qquad f\longmapsto s\circ f\circ t,
$$

is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$. For any complexes $\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet$ let $\mathcal L^\bullet[-n]$ be the shift, $(\mathcal L[-n])^p=\mathcal L^{p-n}$, $d_{\mathcal L[-n]}=(-1)^n d_{\mathcal L}$. By the formula of [def-pur-hom-complex], $\mathcal Hom^k(\mathcal L^\bullet[-n],\mathcal M^\bullet)=\mathcal Hom^{k+n}(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)$ with literally the same differentials in degrees $k=-1,0$ (in degree $k$ both are $f\mapsto d_{\mathcal M}f-(-1)^{k+n}f\,d_{\mathcal L}$), so $H^n(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)))=H^0(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet[-n],\mathcal M^\bullet)))$, compatibly with pre- and postcomposition by morphisms of complexes. Restriction to $\mathcal C/U$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], so it commutes with cohomology sheaves and $s|_U$, $t[-n]|_U$ are quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]; hence $Q_U(s|_U)$ and $Q_U(t[-n]|_U)$ are isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local], applied to $(\mathcal L^\bullet[-n],(\mathcal I')^\bullet)$ and to $((\mathcal L')^\bullet[-n],\mathcal I^\bullet)$ (both targets K-injective), the map $f\mapsto s\circ f\circ t$ on $H^n(\Gamma(U,-))$ becomes, since $Q_U$ is a functor and the bijection is $[f]\mapsto Q_U(f)$, the map $\varphi\mapsto Q_U(s|_U)\circ\varphi\circ Q_U(t[-n]|_U)$ between Hom sets of $D(\mathcal O_U)$, which is bijective. So the displayed morphism induces isomorphisms $H^n(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,(\mathcal I')^\bullet)))\to H^n(\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet((\mathcal L')^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)))$ for all $U$ and $n$, compatible with restriction.

For a complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], the cohomology sheaf $H^n(\mathcal K^\bullet)$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto H^n(\Gamma(U,\mathcal K^\bullet))$: the presheaf kernel, image and quotient are formed sectionwise, and module sheafification is exact and the identity on sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], so it carries the presheaf cohomology to $\operatorname{Ker}d^n/\operatorname{Im}d^{n-1}$ computed in $\Mod(\mathcal O)$, naturally in $\mathcal K^\bullet$. By Step 1 the displayed morphism induces an isomorphism of these presheaves for both Hom complexes, hence an isomorphism of their sheafifications $H^n$ for every $n$; i.e. it is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].
